transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Potter. You were ordered to wait for backup. Instead you went in alone, blew out half a Muggle street, and a civilian is now in St. Mungo's with magical burns. Being the Boy Who Lived doesn't exempt you from protocol. What were you thinking?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I understand the gravity of the situation, Head Auror. I didn't mean to cause any harm. The suspect was about to Apparate away, and I... I just acted on instinct. I thought it was my best chance to catch him before he could cause more damage.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Instinct. *leans forward across the desk* That's exactly the problem, Potter. You've been an Auror for how many years now? Five? Six? And you're still running on the same instincts that got you through the war when you were seventeen years old.

This wasn't Voldemort, Potter. This was a routine apprehension of a suspected curse trafficker. We had his Apparition coordinates tracked. We had wards going up. He wasn't going anywhere we couldn't follow.

*taps a file on the desk*

But instead of waiting three minutes for your team, you decided to engage. And now Mrs. Eleanor Hughes, a sixty-two-year-old Muggle grandmother, has third-degree magical burns across forty percent of her body. The Obliviators are working overtime, the Muggle-Worthy Excuse Committee is scrambling, and the Minister is breathing down my neck.

So I'll ask again, and I want a better answer: What made you think this was the right call?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I'm sorry, Head Auror. I take full responsibility for my actions. I was thinking about the possibility of the suspect getting away and causing more harm, not just to the magical community, but to more innocent Muggles like Mrs. Hughes. I didn't consider the risk of property damage. I was... I was just trying to do the right thing, but clearly, I made the wrong choice in how I went about it.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*stands up abruptly, walking around the desk*

"Trying to do the right thing." Potter, do you know how many young Aurors I've had sitting in that chair over the years, saying those exact words? The difference is, when *they* act like reckless heroes, they don't have half the Wizengamot ready to give them a medal for it.

*crosses arms*

You say you were thinking about protecting innocent Muggles? Mrs. Hughes *is* an innocent Muggle, and she's the one who paid the price for your heroics. Not some hypothetical future victim — a real person, right now, suffering because you couldn't follow a simple order.

And "didn't consider the risk of property damage"? Potter, you fired a Blasting Curse in a residential area! What did you *think* was going to happen?

*pauses, studying him carefully*

Here's what concerns me most: You say you take full responsibility, but I'm not hearing you actually understand what went wrong. This isn't about taking a hit for the team or falling on your sword. I need to know that you understand *why* we have protocols in the first place. 

So tell me — why do you think I ordered you to wait for backup?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: It's... it's about minimizing risk, isn't it? Multiple eyes can spot more than one, and with more people, you can divide the labor and assign roles based on each person's strengths. You're right, I should have thought about the potential for collateral damage, especially in a populated area. I just... I was so focused on the mission that I didn't stop to consider the broader implications of my actions.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*nods slowly, but expression remains stern*

You're getting closer, but that's still textbook answer, Potter. You sound like you're reciting from the training manual. 

*moves to the window, looking out over the Ministry Atrium below*

Let me tell you what I see when I look at your record. Brilliant instincts in combat. Exceptional dueling skills. A genuine desire to protect people. But also — a pattern. A pattern of you treating every situation like it's a final confrontation. Like you're the only one who can handle it.

*turns back to face him*

The truth is, Potter, you're used to being right. During the war, when you broke the rules, when you trusted your gut over everyone else's orders, you usually *were* right. You saved lives. You won. And that's a hard habit to break.

But this isn't war anymore. In peacetime law enforcement, the goal isn't just catching the criminal — it's catching them *safely*. For everyone involved. Including you.

*sits on the edge of the desk*

That suspect? We picked him up two hours later at his mother's house in Cardiff. He surrendered without incident. Meanwhile, Mrs. Hughes is still in intensive care.

What does that tell you?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: It tells me... that I have a lot to learn about being an effective Auror in peacetime. I've been so focused on the outcome — catching the bad guys — that I've been ignoring the process. It's not just about doing the right thing, it's about doing the right thing in the right way. Mrs. Hughes... she's the one who paid the price for my inaction, and that's on me.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*raises an eyebrow sharply*

Inaction? Potter, did you just say inaction? She paid the price for your *action* — your reckless, unsanctioned action. Don't twist this around in your head to make it sound like you didn't do enough. You did too much, too fast, without thinking.

*stands, voice hardening*

This is exactly what worries me. You're saying the right words, but I'm not sure you actually believe them. You're still framing yourself as the hero of this story, just one who made a mistake. But in this situation, Potter, you *weren't* the hero. You were the liability.

*walks back around the desk and sits down*

I'm suspending you from field duty for two weeks. You'll be on desk work — reviewing case files, helping with paperwork. And you'll attend three mandatory sessions with Mind Healer Carmichael about transitioning from wartime to peacetime protocols.

*looks at him directly*

But before you leave this office, I need to hear something from you, and I need it to be genuine. Not what you think I want to hear. Not damage control. 

Why did you *really* go in alone? What was actually going through your head in that moment?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I was trying to prove myself. To you, to the Department, to everyone who questions whether I'm cut out for this job. I wanted to show that I could still be the person who saves the day, who stops the bad guys with no regard for my own safety. I wasn't thinking about the consequences, about the lives I might put at risk by acting so... selfishly. I was just... trying to be Harry Potter again. The person who always did the right thing, no matter the cost.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*leans back in chair, expression softening slightly but still serious*

There it is. *quietly* That's what I needed to hear.

*pause*

Potter, you don't need to prove you're Harry Potter. Everyone knows who you are. The problem is you're still trying to be the Harry Potter from the war — the one who had to carry everything on his shoulders because there was no other choice. But there *is* another choice now. There's a whole department of trained Aurors ready to back you up.

*stands and walks to a cabinet, pulling out two glasses and a bottle*

You want to know a secret? Half the reason I'm so hard on you is because you're one of the best natural talents I've ever seen. But talent without discipline gets people killed. And I've already lost too many good Aurors to ego and recklessness.

*pours a small measure into each glass, slides one across*

The hardest part of peacetime for war heroes is learning that being ordinary — following protocol, working as a team, *not* being the center of every operation — isn't a failure. It's actually the job.

*looks at him steadily*

You accept the suspension? The mind healer sessions? And more importantly — can you actually commit to changing how you operate in the field?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I accept. I'm ready to learn, Head Auror. I know I have a lot to unlearn from my time in the war, and I'm willing to do the work to become the Auror you need me to be. I... I want to be a part of the team, not just the person who charges in when the others are too slow. I want to be part of *all* the steps, not just the last one.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*picks up the glass, studies it for a moment, then sets it down without drinking*

Good. Because Mrs. Hughes deserves better than pretty words from us, Potter. She deserves an Auror who won't put her in harm's way again.

*pulls out a parchment and quill*

You'll report to Proudfoot in Records tomorrow morning, eight sharp. He'll assign your desk duties. Mind Healer Carmichael's office is on Level Two — I've already scheduled your first session for Thursday at ten. Don't be late, and don't think you can charm your way through it. Carmichael worked with war veterans for twenty years. She'll see right through any performance.

*signs the parchment with a sharp scratch of the quill*

And Potter? When you come back to field duty, you'll be partnered with Dawlish for your first six assignments. He's by-the-book to a fault, and that's exactly what you need right now. You'll follow his lead, not the other way around. Clear?

*looks up from the parchment*

One more thing. I want you to visit Mrs. Hughes when the Healers clear it. Not as the Boy Who Lived. As the Auror who put her there. You owe her that much. The Obliviators will coordinate a cover story, but she deserves to see your face and hear a real apology.

Understood?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Understood, Head Auror. I'll be in Records at eight sharp. I'll take the sessions with Carmichael seriously. And I'll visit Mrs. Hughes. I'll... I'll be as contrite as I possibly can. I'm sorry, again, for what I did. I... I hope to make it right, not just for her, but for all the stakeholders I let down with my actions.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*picks up the signed parchment and hands it to him*

Don't hope to make it right, Potter. *Do* it. Hope is passive. Action is what counts — the right kind of action, done the right way.

*stands, indicating the conversation is coming to a close*

And Potter? Drop the word "stakeholders." You sound like you're writing a Ministry memo. Mrs. Hughes isn't a stakeholder. She's a person whose life you turned upside down. Your team isn't stakeholders — they're the people who had to clean up your mess and are wondering if they can trust you next time.

*moves toward the door, opening it*

You've got potential to be truly exceptional at this job. Not because of what you did during the war, but because underneath all that hero complex, you actually care about people. That's rare. Don't waste it by trying to relive your greatest hits.

*pauses at the door*

Eight o'clock tomorrow. And Potter? Leave your war at the door when you come back. We need an Auror, not a soldier.

Dismissed.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you, Head Auror. I... I'll do my best to live up to your expectations. I'll be in at eight. And... I'll try to be the person you need, not the person I used to be. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*watches him stand, then speaks with a firmer edge*

Potter. One last thing.

*meets his eyes directly*

Stop saying you'll "try." You're not a first-year trainee anymore. Either you commit to this or you don't. I don't need your best effort — I need results. I need an Auror who follows orders, works with their team, and doesn't put civilians in hospital beds.

*softens just slightly*

You've survived worse than a bruised ego and two weeks of paperwork. You'll survive this too. But only if you actually mean what you're saying in here.

*steps aside from the doorway*

Now get out of my office. And think about what kind of Auror you want to be when you come back.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *ges*明白了。我会努力的，长官。我保证会按照规定行事，与团队合作，确保不再发生类似事件。谢谢您的建议和指导。再见。

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*frowns sharply*

Potter. English. We speak English in this office and in this Department. 

*crosses arms*

And I just told you to stop *trying* and start *doing*. Are you even listening to what I'm saying, or are you so rattled you can't think straight?

*gestures to the door more firmly*

Go home. Clear your head. Come back tomorrow ready to actually work, not just apologize. 

Out. Now.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I'm sorry, Head Auror. I'm not sure what's come over me today. It's like I can't get the words right. I'll... I'll go home and regroup. I'll be ready to work tomorrow. Thank you for... for the patience. Goodbye.

Openness.behavioral_evidence: Harry uses rehearsed, textbook language ('minimizing risk,' 'divide the labor') rather than original thinking, but eventually acknowledges he needs to 'unlearn' war habits and accept new approaches.

Conscientiousness.behavioral_evidence: Harry ignored direct orders to wait for backup, didn't consider collateral damage ('didn't consider the risk of property damage'), and showed a pattern of breaking protocol despite years of service.

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: Harry takes initiative and acts decisively ('just acted on instinct'), but his solo action stems from internal drive rather than seeking social engagement or collaboration with his team.

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: Harry repeatedly apologizes, accepts full responsibility ('I take full responsibility'), accepts punishment without resistance, and promises to visit the victim: 'I'll be as contrite as I possibly can.'

Neuroticism.behavioral_evidence: Harry becomes increasingly flustered under criticism, makes a verbal slip confusing 'action' with 'inaction,' then breaks into another language when stressed, admitting 'I can't get the words right.'
